milestones.finding: The output of the registered prefill f16w_f32a_tiled kernel violates the independent F64 dot-product oracle. M=3,N=5,K=7, output[0]=0, expected=-0.15974238558624165. This is an operator boundary; no independent whole-model first-divergence capture has been performed.
milestones.hypothesis: Multiple invocations write separate components of each shared vec4. A dynamic component write can lower to a read/modify/write of the whole vector, losing components written by other invocations. Assigning each complete shared vector to one invocation should remove the loss without changing arithmetic or dispatch.

milestones.finding: Exact integer M=4,N=4,K=1 outer product produced 15 zeros and only the final expected output 28. Independent expected values are [2,3,5,7,4,6,10,14,6,9,15,21,8,12,20,28].

Cross-invocation dynamic component writes to workgroup vec4 arrays lose shared-tile components on this Metal runtime. Giving each whole vector one writer corrects the exact integer outer product and all seven unchanged F64 parity cases. Specific compiler lowering to read/modify/write is a mechanism inference, not inspected backend IR.
milestones.numeric_result: All seven existing test shapes pass; worst absolute error 5.348259279891465e-7 under unchanged tolerance.

milestones.finding: Single-writer whole-vector staging passes the original physical F64 kernel tests, the exact integer minimal reproduction, and deterministic supplied application control after official identity regeneration. This is an actual kernel correction, not a disabled-path workaround.
